title: Residual income · four independent calculations (VIM, NMP, SWI, EVA)
body: Four independent questions on residual income and EVA. Each question gives its own data.

questions.q: Vertically Integrated Manufacturing (VIM) has total assets of $3,000,000, financed with twice as much debt as equity. Pretax cost of debt is 6% and cost of equity is 10%. EBIT is $300,000 and the tax rate is 40%. Using the equity charge method, VIM’s residual income is closest to:

New Market Products (NMP) has total assets of $450,000,000, 90% financed with debt (8% pretax), cost of equity 12%, pretax income of $5.1 million (after interest) and a tax rate of 40%. NMP’s residual income is closest to:
questions.why: A is correct. Net income = 5.1 × 0.6 = 3.06m; equity charge = 45m × 12% = 5.4m; RI = −$2.34 million. Interest is already deducted in pretax income.

questions.q: Smithson–Williams Industries (SWI) earned NOPAT of €10 million on total assets of €100 million. Half the assets are debt (9% pretax), cost of equity is 12% and the tax rate is 40%. SWI’s residual income is closest to:
questions.why: A is correct. WACC = 0.5 × 0.09 × 0.6 + 0.5 × 0.12 = 8.7% < NOPAT/assets of 10%; RI = (10% − 8.7%) × 100m = €1.3 million.

title: Residual income · four independent calculations (net income, ROE, EVA and MVA of Sundanci)
body: Four independent questions on residual income, EVA and MVA. Each question gives its own data.
note: Essay questions converted to multiple choice (options written from the quiz feedback); intro lines written for grouping.

questions.q: Net income is €5.00 per share, dividends are €1.00, beginning book value of equity is €30.00 and the required return on equity is 11%. Residual income per share is closest to:
questions.why: A is correct. RI = net income − equity charge = 5.00 − 0.11 × 30.00 = €1.70; dividends are irrelevant.

questions.q: Return on equity is 18%, the required return on equity is 12% and beginning book value of equity is €30.00. Residual income per share is closest to:
Sundanci’s adjusted NOPAT for fiscal 2020 is $100 million, total capital is $700 million (no debt) and the cost of equity is 14%. EVA is closest to:
questions.why: A is correct. EVA = 100 − 14% × 700 = $2 million; with no debt the only capital cost is the cost of equity.

questions.q: Sundanci’s closing share price is $26, 84 million shares are outstanding and total capital is $700 million. Market value added is closest to:
questions.why: A is correct. MVA = market value of capital − total capital = 26 × 84 = 2,184 − 700 = $1,484 million ($17.67 per share).

title: Residual income · intrinsic value examples (VIM, Palmetto Steel, Protected Steel, Notable Books)
body: Four independent questions on residual income models. Each question gives its own data.
note: Essay questions converted to multiple choice (options written from the quiz feedback); intro lines written for grouping.

questions.q: VIM has total assets of $3,000,000 (twice as much debt as equity), pretax cost of debt 6%, cost of equity 10%, EBIT of $300,000 expected indefinitely, tax rate 40%, book value per share $20 and 50,000 shares. The residual income model value per share is closest to:
questions.why: A is correct. RI = $8,000 or $0.16 per share forever; PV = 0.16/0.10 = $1.60; value = 20 + 1.60 = $21.60.

questions.q: Palmetto Steel pays out 80% of earnings, has ROE of 15%, required return 12% and long-term growth 3%. The justified P/B consistent with the residual income model is closest to:
Protected Steel has a book value of $6 per share, earns $0.60 per share forever, pays out all earnings and has a required return of 12%. Its value per share is:
options: $5.00 under both the dividend discount model and the residual income model.
$5.00 under the DDM and $6.00 under the residual income model.

questions.q: Notable Books has a book value of $10 per share, earns $2.00 per share forever, pays out all earnings and has a required return of 12.5%. Its value per share is:
options: $16 under both the DDM and the residual income model.
$10 under the residual income model and $16 under the DDM.

title: Residual income · Simonson Investment Trust and Foodsco
body:
Simonson Investment Trust International (SITI) is expected to earn $4.00, $5.00, and $8.00 per share for the next three years. SITI will pay annual dividends of $2.00, $2.50, and $20.50 in each of these years. The last dividend includes a liquidating payment to shareholders at the end of Year 3 when the trust terminates. SITI’s book value is $8 per share and its required return on equity is 10%.

Foodsco Incorporated (FI), a leading distributor of food products and materials to restaurants and other institutions, has a remarkably steady track record in terms of both return on equity and growth. At year-end 2017, FI had a book value of $30 per share. For the foreseeable future, the company is expected to achieve a ROE of 15% (on trailing book value) and to pay out one-third of its earnings in dividends. The required return is 12%.
note: Essay questions converted to multiple choice (options written from the quiz feedback); intro lines written for grouping.

questions.q: The current value per share of SITI according to the dividend discount model is closest to:
Using book values and residual incomes (3.20, 4.00, 6.75), the residual income model value of SITI is closest to:
SITI’s returns on equity for Years 1 to 3 (net income / beginning book value) are closest to:
questions.why: A is correct. 4.00/8.00 = 50%; 5.00/10.00 = 50%; 8.00/12.50 = 64%. (ROE − r) of 40%, 40% and 54% gives the same residual incomes.

title: Residual income · Thales (justified P/B inputs) and Hottest Topic Stores
body:
Thales S.A. (Paris: HO.PA) has a current stock price of €98.73. It also has book value per share of €26.83 and a P/B of 3.68. Assume that the single-stage growth model is appropriate for valuing the company. Thales S.A.’s adjusted beta is 0.68, the risk-free rate is 4.46%, and the equity risk premium is 5.50%.

Retail fund manager Seymour Simms is considering the purchase of shares in upstart retailer Hottest Topic Stores (HTR). The current book value of HTS is $20 per share, and its market price is $35. Simms expects long-term ROE to be 18%, long-term growth to be 10%, and cost of equity to be 14%.
note: Essay questions converted to multiple choice (options written from the quiz feedback); intro lines written for grouping.

questions.q: If the growth rate is 5.50% and the ROE is 20%, the justified P/B for Thales is closest to:
If the growth rate is 5.50%, the ROE required to yield Thales’s current P/B of 3.68 is closest to:
questions.why: A is correct. Solving 3.68 = 1 + (ROE − 0.082)/(0.082 − 0.055) gives ROE = 15.4%.

questions.q: If the ROE is 20%, the growth rate required for Thales to have its current P/B of 3.68 is closest to:
questions.why: A is correct. Solving 3.68 = 1 + (0.20 − 0.082)/(0.082 − g) gives g = 3.8%.

questions.q: Using a single-stage residual income model, Simms would most likely conclude that HTR’s shares are:
options: somewhat undervalued (value $40 against a price of $35).
somewhat overvalued (value $30 against a price of $35).

title: Residual income · four independent items (DMH, Southern Trust, Industrias Gómez, Lendex OCI)
body: Four independent questions on residual income valuation. Each question gives its own data.
note: Essay questions converted to multiple choice (options written from the quiz feedback); intro lines written for grouping.

questions.q: Dayton Manufactured Homes (DMH) is expected to maintain a ROE of 15% and growth of 10%. It has a book value of $30 per share and a required return on equity of 12%. The single-stage residual income value per share is closest to:

Southern Trust Bank has B0 = $10 per share, ROE of 15% for the next five years with all earnings reinvested (10% thereafter), cost of equity of 10% and a 20% premium over book value at the end of five years (ending book value $20.14). The finite-horizon residual income value per share is closest to:
questions.why: A is correct. V0 = 10 + 2.51 (PV of five residual incomes) + 0.20 × 20.14/1.10⁵ (2.50) = $15.01.

questions.q: Industrias Gómez has a current book value of €20.00 per share, expected EPS of €1.50, 2.50, 3.50, 4.50 and 5.50, dividends of €1.00 for three years and €2.00 for two years, a terminal price of 14× trailing earnings and a required return of 9%. The value per share is closest to:
options: €55.29 under both the residual income model and the dividend discount model.
€30.22 under the residual income model and €50.05 under the DDM.
questions.why: A is correct. Residual incomes: −0.300, 0.655, 1.520, 2.295, 3.070 (PV 5.071); terminal premium 77.00 − 30.50 = 46.50 (PV 30.22); 20.00 + 5.071 + 30.222 = €55.293. The DDM gives the same value.

questions.q: Lendex Electronics has had negative other comprehensive income from available-for-sale securities in each of the past five years. Kent should most likely:
options: adjust income downward by the other comprehensive income losses, lowering ROE; book value is not misstated.
leave income as reported because the losses bypass the income statement.
add the losses back to book value.
questions.why: A is correct. Persistently negative OCI that bypasses the income statement is a recurring cost; book value already reflects it through accumulated other comprehensive income.

title: Residual income · Procter & Gamble (Kobayashi): eight-year RI valuation and DDM
body:
Shunichi Kobayashi is valuing Procter & Gamble Company (NYSE: PG). Kobayashi has made the following assumptions:

Book value per share is estimated at $21.30 on 31 March 2019.

EPS will be 18% of the beginning book value per share for the next eight years.

Cash dividends paid will be 70% of EPS.

At the end of the eight-year period, the market price per share will be four times the book value per share.

The beta for PG is 0.50, the risk-free rate is 2.0%, and the equity risk premium is 6.2%.

The current market price of PG is $107.50, which indicates a current P/B of 5.05.
note: Essay questions converted to multiple choice (options written from the quiz feedback); intro lines written for grouping.

questions.q: The ending book value per share at the end of Year 8 is closest to:
The Year 1 residual income per share is closest to:
The value per share of PG using the residual income model is closest to:
The value per share of PG using the dividend discount model compared with the residual income estimate is:
options: lower, because dividends are paid later.
higher, because dividends are not discounted.
questions.why: A is correct. PV of eight dividends 20.634 + PV of terminal price 129.767 (87.165) = $107.80. With the same assumptions the two models agree even though they recognize value at different times.
